column3: The Hebrew says David spoke “to his heart”; BSB uses “to himself.” The escape verb is emphatically repeated in Hebrew but appears once in BSB.
The Hebrew calls Abigail “Nabal’s wife”; BSB specifies “the widow of Nabal.”
The Hebrew says passively that Saul was told; BSB uses active “Saul learned.”
The Hebrew requests that unnamed people “give me a place”; BSB makes this passive “let me be assigned a place.”
The Hebrew repeats Ziklag’s name as belonging to Judah’s kings; BSB uses “it.”
The Hebrew’s time expression literally uses “days and four months”; BSB renders the period as “a year and four months.”
The Hebrew uses collective singular names for the Geshurite, Girzite, and Amalekite; BSB uses plural ethnic names.
The Hebrew separately says David returned and came to Achish; BSB combines these as “return to Achish.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Achish as questioner and joins the three Negev regions with “and”; BSB uses a relative clause for Achish and separates the answers with “or.”
The Hebrew describes the territory as “the field of the Philistines”; BSB uses “Philistine territory.”
The Hebrew introduces Achish’s words with “saying”; BSB uses “thinking.”
